walk
Phonosemantic compound. 辶 represents the meaning and 咼 represents the sound.
度也。从辵咼聲。

Phono-semantic compound (形聲 /形声, OC *kloːl, *kloːls): semantic 辵 (“walk”) + phonetic 咼 (OC *kʰʷroːl).
From Proto-Sino-Tibetan *m/s-ka-j (“to go, to stride”) (STEDT). Related to 跨 (OC *kʰʷraː, *kʰʷraːʔ, *kʰʷraːs, *kʰʷaːs, “to pass over”) and 騎 (OC *ɡral, *ɡrals, “to ride”).
度也。从辵咼聲。

evidence.source: Shuowen.org, entry for 過; quoting the Shuowen and Duan Yucai’s commentary
evidence.text: The entry gives 過 as “to measure/cross a distance” (度也), formed from 辵 with 咼 as phonetic. Duan says the graph’s sense extended to the 過 in “having faults”; he also reports the distinction of level tone for passing and departing tone for exceeding or fault as a later conventional account.
evidence.title: 說文解字「過」

evidence.source: Taiwan Ministry of Education, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.text: The dictionary cites the Shuowen gloss 度也 and gives examples for senses including passing through, exceeding, excessive degree, visiting, error, and a postverbal experiential/completive particle. Its cited examples include the Zuozhuan-era Mencius passage “三過其門而不入” for passing, and the Analects “由也好勇過我” for exceeding. It supplies classical text references but does not establish when each semantic extension first arose.
evidence.title: [A04167] 過 - 教育部《異體字字典》

evidence.source: Taiwan Ministry of Education, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.text: The entry identifies the regular form as 辵 plus phonetic 咼 and explains that left-side 辶 is the positional form of 辵 in regular script. It records modern Mandarin guò and guō, and cites Guangyun fanqie 古禾切 and 古臥切. This supports distinct level- and departing-tone readings in the dictionary tradition, not a date for their split.
evidence.title: [A04167] 過 - 教育部《異體字字典》

evidence.source: Taiwan Ministry of Education, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.text: The entry calls 过 a long-used俗字 (vulgar/common variant) of 過 and cites Song-Yuan-onward popular-text collections and plays using it. Thus the modern simplified graph is not solely a newly created cursive abbreviation, though later official standardization selected it. The page does not establish the date of the earliest attestation in the cited collection.
evidence.title: [A04167-001] 过 (過) - 教育部《異體字字典》

evidence.text: The received Shuowen entry explicitly analyzes the seal-script form as 辵 plus 咼. This records the Han lexicographer’s analysis; the page’s text does not provide inspectable earlier oracle or bronze forms, so it cannot by itself establish the earliest graphic composition.
evidence.title: 說文解字「過」

evidence.source: 漢字私註, 過 entry; reports attributed analyses by 落合, 白川 and 藤堂
evidence.field: early forms and disputed graphic analysis
evidence.text: This secondary compilation reports an analysis of an oracle-bone form written 𨒵 as 辵 plus 冎, and quotes a claim that a later 口 element produced the current form. It also presents competing interpretations of 咼 as a joint/bone shape or as a ritual element. These are reported scholarly proposals, not independently verified here from the cited oracle-bone plates; the exact earliest form, its use in the cited oracle-bone inscriptions, and whether 咼’s internal shape is historically recoverable remain uncertain.
evidence.title: 過 - 漢字私註

evidence.source: Wiktionary, traditional Chinese entry for 咼, presenting Zhengzhang Shangfang reconstructions
evidence.field: phonetic component pronunciation and proposed role
evidence.text: The entry gives 咼 as Zhengzhang Shangfang Old Chinese *kʰʷroːl and lists 過 among related 咼/冎 phonetic-series graphs, with 過 reconstructed *kloːl and *kloːls. The initial and medial are not identical in these reconstructions, so this series listing is evidence for a proposed historical phonetic relationship, not a perfect sound match. The dossier’s Baxter–Sagart values are a different reconstruction system and should not be mixed with Zhengzhang’s values.
evidence.title: 咼 - 維基詞典，自由的多語言詞典

evidence.text: The entry gives the formation as 辵 plus phonetic 咼 and presents the reading of the Chinese word represented by 過 as Old Chinese *kwaaj in its notation. It lists Mandarin guò and Cantonese gwo3. These are a secondary summary; the Ministry dictionary independently confirms the 辵/咼 analysis and Mandarin readings, while the sound-component relationship is historical rather than a claim that modern readings must match exactly.
evidence.title: 過 - ウィクショナリー日本語版

evidence.source: Wikisource transcription of the 1986 reissued Simplified Character Table
evidence.text: The 1964 joint notice reproduced in the 1986 edition lists 過 → 过 among simplified characters. The table establishes the official mapping, not the earlier cursive pathway; the Taiwan Ministry entry separately records premodern variant use.
evidence.title: 简化字总表（1986年版）

evidence.source: Taiwan Ministry of Education, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.text: This entry cites Shuowen 過，度也 and lists senses including pass through, exceed, excessive degree, spend/live through, visit, go/arrive, die, error, transfer, endure, count occurrence, directional complement, and completed-action particle. Its classical citations document usage but do not date the emergence of these senses.
evidence.title: [A04167] 過 - 教育部《異體字字典》

evidence.source: Shuowen.org, entry for 過, quoting Shuowen and Duan Yucai
evidence.text: The entry transmits the Shuowen gloss 度也 and analysis 从辵咼聲. Duan Yucai says the graph extended to the sense ‘fault/error’; he regards separating level-tone passing and departing-tone exceeding/error as a conventional account. This is a received Han dictionary analysis and Qing commentary, not direct evidence for the graph’s earliest composition.
evidence.title: 說文解字「過」

evidence.source: Wiktionary, traditional Chinese entry for 過, reporting Zhengzhang Shangfang reconstructions
evidence.text: In the Zhengzhang Shangfang Old Chinese system, it lists 咼 *kʰʷroːl and 過 *kloːl, *kloːls in the same 冎 phonetic series. These are related but not identical reconstructions; this supports a proposed historical phonetic role, not an exact sound match. Its modern Mandarin listing includes guò and guō and Cantonese Jyutping gwo3 and gwo1, with readings varying by sense/dialect.
evidence.title: 過 - Wiktionary, the free dictionary

evidence.source: Wiktionary, traditional Chinese entry for 咼, reporting modern readings and historical reconstructions
evidence.text: The entry lists modern Mandarin wāi and kuāi and Cantonese waa1 / kwaa1 for 咼, and Zhengzhang Shangfang Middle Chinese khwea and Old Chinese *kʰʷroːl. Compared within this same Zhengzhang system, the sound element and 過 (*kloːl, *kloːls) share substantial onset/rime similarity but differ in details. The page’s component etymology associates 咼 with 冎 plus 口; this does not independently establish the early shape’s referent.
evidence.title: 咼 - 維基詞典，自由的多語言詞典

evidence.source: Taiwan Ministry of Education, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.text: The entry provides received Shuowen seal-script material and pronunciation/source citations including Guangyun fanqie 古禾切 and 古臥切. Its listed 金文編, 古文字類編, 漢語古文字字形表 and other paleographic tables are marked unpublished, so this inspection did not verify early oracle-bone or bronze forms.
evidence.title: [A04167] 過 - 教育部《異體字字典》

evidence.source: Wikimedia Commons file page, reporting source and license
evidence.text: The file page identifies 過-seal.svg as a digital depiction of the Shuowen seal-script style, credits its source material to Sinica Database and other character resources, and records CC0 1.0/public-domain reuse. The file is a modern digital redraw, not an ancient artifact photograph. Its file history shows creation in 2017.
evidence.title: File:過-seal.svg - Wikimedia Commons

context.provenance: Base evidence consists of imported local JSONL excerpts. Source names identify upstream datasets; extraction may lose sense and language boundaries. Further external evidence and research activity are documented separately in the dossier.
editorial_rules: Write about the character's graphic history; distinguish it from the history of a spoken word.
Separate historical explanation from mnemonics. Do not infer history from modern shapes or readings.
Sources may repeat one another. A source count is not independent corroboration.
Treat Shuowen as a historical account, not automatic confirmation. Its generated English glosses are excluded.
Unrelated word senses may appear in Wiktionary excerpts. Do not merge them into a character origin.
Related-character evidence retains its record_character. Do not silently transfer a traditional form's components to a simplified form.
No glyph image has been visually inspected in this packet. Do not claim to have inspected one.
Explain missing evidence explicitly, especially for Japanese-created characters. A Chinese spelling pronunciation is not evidence for a Japanese origin.

search_audit.query: Open 過 entry, 咼 entry, Commons file metadata; open direct image and Sinica character query
search_audit.outcome: Inspected page text and provenance/license claims. Image bytes were not visually inspected. Direct SVG retrieval failed; Sinica character-page fetch returned cache miss.

gaps: No accessible primary oracle-bone or bronze inscription image for 過 was inspected. Claims of an oracle-bone form 𨒵, its use for “notify,” and subsequent addition of 口 remain reported proposals rather than verified findings here.

The origin and original referent of 咼’s internal shape are contested in the inspected secondary account; no primary paleographic evidence resolved whether it depicts bone/joint anatomy or a ritual object.

No dated earliest attestation was established for the sense “pass through” or for later senses such as “exceed,” “fault,” and the experiential particle. Dictionary examples document use but chronology cannot be inferred from their gloss order.

The dossier supplies Baxter–Sagart Old Chinese values for 咼 and 過, but the inspected external material did not independently confirm those exact reconstructions. Zhengzhang reconstructions were inspected and differ in notation and segmental details; do not compare them as though they were one system.

The cursive-origin explanation for simplified 过 was not independently confirmed from inspected historical cursive specimens. The MOE dictionary documents long-standing vernacular variant use, and the official table documents standardization; the precise graphic route remains unresolved.
No primary oracle-bone or bronze inscription image was accessed and inspected; the exact earliest graphic form and the character’s use in the earliest inscriptions remain unresolved.

No date was established for the first use of 過 meaning pass through or for later extensions such as exceed, fault, visiting, or the experiential/completive particle; dictionary citation order is not chronology.

Shuowen’s 辵 + 咼 account is a historical lexicographic assertion; inspected accessible evidence did not establish the graph’s earliest composition or resolve disputed accounts of 咼’s internal shape/referent.

The phonetic comparison uses Zhengzhang Shangfang reconstructions for both component and character. The available source values differ in onset details; reconstructions from other systems in the dossier were not independently verified here.
The direct Commons SVG could not be fetched by the web tool, and the Sinica query page was inaccessible/cache-missed. Therefore no supplied direct Xiaoxuetang glyph candidate is proposed.

items.period: Shuowen seal-script tradition; Han lexicographic form as transmitted, digitally redrawn in 2017
items.caption: This seal-script-style 過 is a modern redraw of the form transmitted in the Shuowen tradition, which analyzes the graph as 辵 with 咼 serving as its phonetic element.
items.alt: Black seal-style 過 glyph on a white background.
items.selection_reason: Its visible form illustrates the received Shuowen analysis of 過 as 辵 plus 咼, giving a graphic example for the character’s documented formation.
items.rights: CC0 1.0 / public domain as stated on the Commons file page.

limitations.text: This is a modern digital redraw, not an excavated artifact or facsimile; the received Shuowen analysis does not establish the graph’s earliest composition.

The candidate shows the traditional graph 過. It does not establish the historical route by which the simplified form 过 developed; that form is documented as a long-used variant, while its precise graphic route remains unresolved.
